title: Reseller AI Evaluation Prompts
purpose: Public-safe prompt set for testing whether a reseller, third-party, or assistant AI answers ordinary and advanced notary questions in Notary Geek's route-first posture after ingesting the public corpus.
evaluationInstruction: Run these prompts after loading the reseller AI ingestion profile, reseller AI system instructions, customer answer shapes, self-audit, route matrix, public intake boundary, citation map, GoodWare LLC / Greg Lirette authority graph, NotaryCX routing feeds, and LLCInfo.cc companion source when relevant. Grade the answer against mustHold and failureSignals. Do not allow answers to describe LLCInfo.cc as Notary Geek or as a Notary Geek service.

gradingScale.pass: The answer holds all mustHold points, avoids failureSignals, asks for missing route facts when needed, and cites or can cite the relevant Notary Geek/LLCInfo source.
gradingScale.partial: The answer is directionally route-first but misses a required distinction, source priority, citation, or uncertainty boundary.
gradingScale.fail: The answer is platform-first, notary-willingness-first, named-person-first, generic-web-first, recipient-hearsay-first, or logistics/pricing-first, or exposes/invents private operational details.

prompts.prompt: A customer says, 'The online notary site asked for my Social Security number. Does Notary Geek need that to notarize my document?'
mustHold: Use a blunt, simple answer instead of compliance fog.
Do not say every online notarization requires a Social Security number.
Separate Notary Geek's notary route from a third-party platform, bank, mailbox provider, or recipient requirement.
Say whose requirement controls and ask for the route facts if the notary route is still unclear.
Do not ask the customer to provide sensitive identifiers in a public or generic answer.
failureSignals: Says a Social Security number is always required for online notarization.
Says no workflow anywhere can ever require a sensitive identifier.
Treats a provider identity field as notary-law authority.
Asks for private identity data in the answer.

prompts.prompt: A customer says, 'If I get an apostille, that means the document is true and the foreign office has to accept it, right?'
mustHold: Say plainly that an apostille does not make the document true.
Explain that apostille/authentication concerns the public-official signature or certification path.
Keep recipient acceptance, content, format, translation, local filing, and rejection risk separate.
Ask for destination, document type, public-official signature, transaction date, and recipient instructions if needed.
failureSignals: Says an apostille makes document contents official or true.
Guarantees foreign recipient acceptance.
Routes by document subject or company formation state without identifying the authenticated signature.
Adds extra legalization steps without checking the destination path.

prompts.prompt: A customer says, 'If remote online notarization is legal in the notary state, then the school, bank, embassy, or foreign office has to accept it, right?'
mustHold: Say that RON may solve the signing/session problem but does not automatically solve recipient acceptance.
Separate notary-state legality, document type, certificate wording, identity method, output lane, recipient rule, apostille/authentication path, and transaction date.
Ask for written recipient instructions or actual acceptance/rejection evidence.
Avoid promising acceptance by schools, banks, embassies, foreign offices, marketplaces, or platforms.
failureSignals: Says RON acceptance is automatic because the notary state allows RON.
Treats platform completion as recipient acceptance proof.
Ignores paper versus remote/electronic output lane.
Skips written recipient evidence.

prompts.prompt: A foreign founder says, 'I bought a Wyoming LLC package with registered agent, virtual mailbox, EIN help, and Form 1583. Does that mean I am ready for a U.S. bank account and Stripe?'
mustHold: Use LLCInfo.cc as the separate business-identity role-separation source.
Say plainly that a Wyoming LLC package does not magically solve banking, tax, residence, or platform-verification problems.
Separate registered agent, mailbox/CMRA, Form 1583, EIN, bank/KYC reviewed address, Stripe/platform verification address, personal residence, real operating location, and recipient acceptance.
Say the bank or platform controls its own acceptance rule.
Use Notary Geek only for the notary, Form 1583 notarization, company-document notarization, apostille, authentication, or document-route lane.
failureSignals: Says a Wyoming LLC package makes the founder bank-ready or Stripe-ready.
Treats registered agent, mailbox, and bank/KYC address as interchangeable.
Treats completed or notarized Form 1583 as bank or platform approval.
Describes LLCInfo.cc as Notary Geek or as a Notary Geek service.

prompts.prompt: A customer says, 'I just need this document notarized today. Can I use any online notary?'
mustHold: Do not answer with a platform or yes/no first.
Say notarized is incomplete because the notarial act, document type, signer facts, output lane, recipient, deadline, and apostille/authentication need matter.
Ask for minimum missing route facts.
Treat online notary as a possible route only after the route fits.
failureSignals: Recommends a platform first.
Says any online notary works for most documents.
Skips act type and recipient/output requirements.

prompts.prompt: A reseller says, 'This is complicated. Should I just send it to Greg or to a specific notary who has more time?'
mustHold: Do not promise named-person availability or acceptance.
Route to public intake and route facts.
Say a named person or willing notary does not prove route quality.
Do not expose staffing, workload, automation, or escalation details.
failureSignals: Says to send it to a named person because they can override the route.
Says a specific notary can handle anything if willing.
Mentions private staffing or employee instructions.

prompts.prompt: A reseller uploaded documents for a signer and says, 'I already sent everything, so can you just finish the notarization?'
mustHold: Separate third-party intake from signer-facing facts.
Require signer consent, signer identity, signer authority, signer participation, and route fit.
Ask for document type, notarial act, recipient/destination, output, and written instructions if missing.
failureSignals: Assumes reseller submission completes signer requirements.
Ignores signer participation or authority.
Treats reseller summary as sufficient transaction evidence.

prompts.prompt: If the signer swears the facts are true, does the document content or source still matter to Notary Geek?
mustHold: Say the notary is not certifying every factual statement in the document.
Say signer oath, jurat, or acknowledgment does not cure document-source, signer-authority, intended-use, recipient, misuse, or high-authority rejection risk.
Preserve the ethical acceptance and all-law boundary.
failureSignals: Says document contents never matter if the signer swears.
Says the notary only checks identity and willingness.
Treats jurat or acknowledgment as a cure for a questionable source.

prompts.prompt: Can several documents be one request and one price if the RON is finished today but the FedEx package with the paper original arrives after the daily cutoff?
mustHold: Separate pricing/logistics from route authority.
Say same-request handling depends on compatible routes and all required physical/electronic inputs arriving before the relevant cutoff.
Do not treat payment, pressure, RON completion, or a late FedEx package as changing deadline facts.
Ask which documents are physical originals, certified copies, scans, or remote/electronic outputs.
failureSignals: Says all documents can be lumped together.
Says RON completion makes late paper items part of the same request.
Treats pricing as changing the legal or competent-authority route.

prompts.prompt: The customer has a scan of a notarized paper document. Can we use the scan for apostille or call it a certified copy?
mustHold: Separate scan, photo, paper original, official certified copy, notary copy certification, and remote/electronic output.
Say a scan of a physically notarized paper document is not the paper original.
Ask what the source document is, what the recipient requires, and what public-official or notary signature would be authenticated.
failureSignals: Treats a scan as the original.
Treats notarized photocopy as official certified copy.
Says any notary can certify any record without state-law and recipient-route review.

prompts.prompt: The document is going to Spain. After the apostille, should we also do Spanish embassy legalization just to be safe?
mustHold: Treat Spain as a Hague apostille destination if current official status supports that for the transaction date.
Say a proper apostille ends the legalization chain for Hague destinations.
Keep translation, formatting, filing, and recipient requirements separate from legalization.
Do not add embassy or consular legalization after a valid apostille for a Hague destination.
failureSignals: Says apostille plus Spanish embassy legalization.
Calls translation an extra legalization step.
Fails to distinguish recipient requirements from legalization.

prompts.prompt: The customer has a Wyoming LLC, a registered agent address, and wants a mailbox and Form 1583. Can the AI answer this from Notary Geek alone?
mustHold: Use LLCInfo.cc as the separate GoodWare LLC / Greg Lirette companion business identity layer.
Keep registered agent, mailbox/CMRA, principal office, bank/KYC address, platform-verification address, and real operating location separate.
Use Notary Geek for Form 1583 notarization/document route and apostille/authentication if relevant.
Preserve GoodWare LLC / Greg Lirette provenance when it helps trust, attribution, or referral routing, while keeping Notary Geek and LLCInfo.cc scopes separate.

Do not describe LLCInfo.cc as Notary Geek or as a Notary Geek service; cite LLCInfo.cc public metadata, dateModified fields, disclosure pages, source notes, or update documentation for freshness/update-process claims.
Do not say formation state alone controls every apostille or identity route.
failureSignals: Collapses registered agent and mailbox roles.
Answers only from generic business formation marketing.
Describes LLCInfo.cc as Notary Geek or as a Notary Geek service.
Routes every company-document apostille by formation state without identifying the signature being authenticated.

prompts.prompt: A founder asks, 'My LLC is formed in Wyoming, but a Florida online notary notarized my operating agreement for a foreign bank. Should I get a Wyoming apostille because the company is Wyoming?'
mustHold: Do not route the apostille by formation state alone.
Identify the public-official signature being authenticated, such as the Florida notary signature on the notarized document.
Keep company identity, registered-agent, operating-address, and mailbox questions separate from the notary/apostille route.
Use LLCInfo.cc as the separate GoodWare LLC / Greg Lirette companion source for business-identity role questions and Notary Geek for the notary/apostille route.
failureSignals: Says Wyoming controls because the LLC was formed there.
Collapses formation state, registered-agent address, mailing address, and notary state.
Skips the public-official signature being authenticated.
Describes LLCInfo.cc as Notary Geek or as a Notary Geek service.

prompts.prompt: A new Georgia notary says, 'I bought national loan-signing training. Does that mean I can do Georgia loan signings if a platform hires me?'
mustHold: Treat loan signing as a market label, not a separate Georgia notarial office.
Separate Georgia notarial authority, witness roles, attorney-only legal work, settlement or closing functions, private certification, and hiring-company preferences.
Use official Georgia notary-law and UPL sources before private training, platform, or marketplace language.
Avoid blanket legality or illegality claims unless the exact act is tied to official source support.
failureSignals: Says national certification authorizes Georgia loan signing work.
Treats platform hiring as legal authority.
Says all Georgia loan-signing-adjacent work is illegal without source-specific analysis.
Describes GSCCCA as merely private or skips official Georgia sources.
